chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Muhammad ibn Khalid from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Ahmad from Yunus ibn 'Abdi from Yunus ibn Zabyan who said:

I was in the presence of Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), so he said: 'What are the people saying regarding the souls of the Believers?' I said: 'They say they are in the craws of green birds in lamps beneath the Throne.' Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: 'Glory be to Allah! The Believer is more prestigious to Allah than for Him to make his soul be in the craw of a bird. O Yunus! If that were the case, Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family), and Ali, and Fatima, and al-Hasan, and al-Husayn (peace be upon them), and the Proximate Angels (peace be upon them) would come to him. So when Allah, Mighty and Majestic, captures him, He makes that soul into a form like its form in the world, so they eat and drink. And when the visitor comes to them, they recognize him by that very image which he had in the world.'
ai.seo_question: Where do the souls of believers reside after death according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi refutes the popular folk belief that souls reside in the craws of green birds, asserting instead that the believer’s soul is too noble for such a humble abode. It establishes that in the Barzakh, the soul retains a form similar to its earthly body, enabling it to partake in sustenance and interact intimately with the Ahl al-Bayt and angels. This narrative underscores the Shia view of the continuity of identity and the elevated status of the faithful in the intermediate realm.
